paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the performance of knowledge probing after editing across various editing methods. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale ranging from approximately 1 to 1000. Tick labels are present at 1, 10, 100, and 1000. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" with a linear scale ranging from approximately 40 to 66. The “Base” line is black with circular markers and a solid line style, starting at approximately 44% and increasing to approximately 51% across the x-axis range. The “FT” line is blue with triangular markers and a solid line style, starting at roughly 39% and rising to approximately 51% over the plotted range. The “IKE” line is red with triangular markers and a solid line style, beginning at approximately 46% and reaching roughly 52% at the highest co-occurrence number. The “MEND” line is purple with diamond markers and a solid line style, starting at approximately 49% and increasing to approximately 56% across the x-axis. The "MEMIT” line is orange with diamond markers and a solid line style, beginning at roughly 48% and reaching approximately 55% at the highest frequency. The "ROME” line is green with square markers and a solid line style, beginning at approximately 51% and increasing to roughly 66% across the plotted range.
